name: $lorenz
documentation:
Chaotic signal source based on the Lorenz strange attractor.

Simulates the Lorenz system continuously — changing any parameter pulls the
trajectory in a new direction rather than restarting from scratch. Outputs x
(default) and y coordinates normalized to **±5V**, and z normalized to **0–5V**
(z is always positive in the Lorenz system).

## Parameters (all 0–5 CV)

| param | mapped range | default | chaotic butterfly |
|-------|-------------|---------|-------------------|
| sigma | σ 0–30      | 1.667 → σ=10   | stays chaotic for σ > 0 |
| rho   | ρ 0–60      | 2.333 → ρ=28   | chaos requires ρ > ~24.74 (CV > ~2.06V) |
| beta  | β 0–10      | 1.333 → β=8/3  | classic shape near 2.667 |
| rate  | 0–200 t/s   | 0.1   → 4 t/s  | audio-rate at ≥ ~50 t/s |

## Example

```js
// Classic Lorenz butterfly at default params
$lorenz()

// Access all three outputs
const l = $lorenz()
l    // x coordinate (±5V)
l.y  // y coordinate (±5V)
l.z  // z coordinate (0–5V)

// Modulate rho — nudges the attractor without resetting it
$lorenz({ rho: $sine('1hz').range(0, 5), rate: 0.5 }).out()
```

beta.description: β, the attractor's shape: 5 is β = 10, and the default is the classic β = 8/3

rate.description: simulation speed: 0 freezes and 5 is fastest; the default traces a slow butterfly, and from about 1.25 the chaos runs at audio rate

rho.description: ρ, how far the attractor's two lobes sit from the centre: 5 is ρ = 60, and the default is ρ = 28; below about 2.06 (ρ ≈ 24.74) the motion settles to a still point

sigma.description: σ, how fast x chases y: 5 is σ = 30, and the default is σ = 10; stays chaotic above 0

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: x coordinate of the attractor, swinging between its two lobes

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: y coordinate, which x chases, so it leads x slightly

outputs.name: z
outputs.description: z coordinate, the attractor's height, pulsing once per loop

name: $swell
documentation:
Ocean swell as CV: the surface of a simulated sea, read at a fixed point.

The sea sums `waves` Gerstner waves. Each moves the water in circles rather
than just up and down, which bunches the surface into sharp crests between
wide, flat troughs — the shape of real swell, set by `steepness`. The first
wave rolls at `freq`; `chop` spreads the others above it, so their crests
drift in and out of line and the sea arrives in sets, with the occasional
wave far bigger than the rest. `spread` scatters their directions.

- **height** (default) — surface height, ±5V. It reaches ±5V only when
  every wave lines up, so a sea with `chop` above 0 usually stays inside it.
- **tilt** — how the surface leans along the swell, the way a moored boat
  pitches: positive while the water rises, negative while it falls. A sine
  at `steepness` 0; when steep, a sawtooth that snaps down at each crest.
- **roll** — the sideways lean from waves arriving off-axis. Silent at
  `spread` 0, and busier as `spread` and `chop` rise.

Every input can be modulated live: the waves bend to the new values without
restarting. Each channel is its own sea.

## Example

```js
// A slow, steep swell sweeping a filter
$lpf($saw('a1'), $swell('0.1hz', { steepness: 4 }).range('200hz', '2000hz')).out()

// A choppy, confused sea: the swell's lean swaying a sine's level
const sea = $swell('0.2hz', { chop: 4, spread: 5, waves: 12 })
$sine('c3').amp(sea.tilt.range(0, 5)).out()
```

chop.description: spectral width: the other waves sit up to `chop / 2` octaves above `freq`; 0 is one clean, periodic swell, higher rolls in sets and adds chop

freq.description: rate of the main swell, e.g. `'0.1hz'`

seed.description: picks the sea: each seed, and each channel, places the waves at different frequencies and directions

spread.description: directional spread: 0 sends every wave the same way, 5 brings them from every direction, a confused sea

steepness.description: crest sharpness: 0 rolls as a sine, 5 peaks into sharp crests over wide, flat troughs

waves.description: number of waves in the sea; waves added or removed by a patch update fade over one swell period

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: water height at a fixed point

outputs.name: tilt
outputs.description: lean along the swell: positive while the water rises

outputs.name: roll
outputs.description: lean across the swell, from waves arriving off-axis

name: $mix
documentation:
Mix module for combining multiple signals into a single mix bus.

Use this when you want to blend several multichannel modulation/audio sources.
It mixes channel `n` across all inputs into output channel `n`, rather than

name: $mixDown
documentation:
Folds a polyphonic input down to an arbitrary target channel count.

Unlike `$mix` (which mixes channel `n` of every input into output channel
`n`), `$mixDown` takes a single poly signal and distributes its `N` channels
across `M` output channels by panning them evenly over the output field with
an equal-power crossfade. With the default `channels = 1` it is a plain mono
sum; `channels = 2` produces an equal-power stereo fold-down. When the target
exceeds the input channel count, the input is instead spread to fill every
output channel (equal-power interpolation) so no channel is left silent.

- **channels** — target output channel count (1–64, default 1)
- **mode** — how channels landing on the same output combine (sum / average /
  max / min); applies only when folding down (target ≤ input channels)

## Example

```js
// Fold a 3-voice spread down to stereo
$saw($spread(0, 5, 3)).mix(2).out()
```

mode.description: how channels landing on the same output combine

outputs.description: the input channels spread evenly across the output channels with equal-power panning

name: $tr808.kick
documentation:
TR-808 bass drum.

A circuit model of the 808's deep, booming kick: a low, round ring at ≈49.5
Hz with a click at the attack and a pitch that sighs down as it rings.
**decay** sets how long it booms, **tone** how much click comes through,
**freq** its pitch, and **accent** how hard it hits.

As on the 808, a hit that lands on a still-ringing one builds on it, so long
decays at fast tempos swing in level from hit to hit; **restart** starts
every hit from rest instead.

An unaccented hit peaks near **±5 V** and a fully accented one near **±10
V**. Near the top of the **freq** range the drum overdrives, so accent adds
less there.

```js
$tr808.kick($clock.beatTrigger, { decay: 4 }).out()
```

accent.description: how hard the hit lands, read at each strike: up to twice as loud at 5 V, with more pitch sigh

decay.description: how long the drum rings, from ≈0.09 s to ≈3.8 s; ≈0.6 s at 2.5

freq.description: pitch; stock is ≈49.5 Hz, and the hit gets louder or quieter far from it

hold.description: sample the controls on each strike and hold them until the next, as accent always is, so changes reach only the hits after them

restart.description: start every hit from rest, fading out one still sounding over 2 ms; off, each hit builds on the last, as on the 808

tone.description: brightness of the attack, from a dull thud to a bright click

signalParams.description: rising edges strike the drum

name: $tr808.hiHat
documentation:
TR-808 hi-hats, closed and open.

A circuit model of the 808's hi-hats: the cymbal's six square waves filtered
to a thin, bright band. **closed** strikes a short, tight hat and **open** a
longer one that rings for as long as **decay** sets; **accent** makes either
hit harder.

hard: below 0 the open hat only ducks, and above 0 it stops dead.

An unaccented hit of either hat peaks near **±5 V** and a fully accented one
near **±10 V**.

name: $comp
documentation:
EXPERIMENTAL

Single-band feed-forward dynamics processor with peak envelope follower.

Two stages run in parallel:

- **downward stage** acts on signal above `threshold`. `ratio > 1` =
  compression, `ratio < 1` = upward expansion (boost loud), `ratio = 1` =
  passthrough.
- **upward stage** acts on signal below `upwardThreshold`. `upwardRatio > 1`
  = upward compression (boost quiet), `upwardRatio < 1` = downward
  expansion / gate-like attenuation of quiet signal, `upwardRatio = 1` =
  passthrough.

Both ratios use textbook `X:1` notation (X = Δinput dB / Δoutput dB) and
are lower-bounded at 1e-3 (≈ Ableton's 1:1000 display). The detected
level is clamped to ±60 dB so expansion stays bounded at signal extremes.

An optional **side-chain** input lets the envelope follower track an
external signal while the gain is applied to `input` — useful for
ducking, kick-triggered pumping, or building multiband effects like OTT.

**Signal flow:** input → input gain → (detector: side-chain or input)
  → up + down compression → output gain → dry/wet mix → output

- **threshold** — downward stage threshold in volts (0–5, default 2.5).
- **ratio** — downward stage ratio in textbook X:1 form. > 1 compresses,
  < 1 expands (boosts loud signal), 1 = passthrough. Lower-bounded at
  1e-3 (≈ 1:1000 expansion); upper bound is `f32::INFINITY` =
  brick-wall limiter. Default 4.0 (= Ableton display 1:0.25).
- **upwardThreshold** — upward stage threshold in volts (0–5, default 0).
- **upwardRatio** — upward stage ratio in textbook X:1 form. > 1 boosts
  quiet signal, < 1 gates quiet signal, 1 = passthrough. Same bounds as
  `ratio`. Default 1 (passthrough).
- **sidechain** — optional external detector signal.
- **attack** / **release** — envelope follower time constants in seconds.
- **makeup** — post-compression makeup gain as a dB-domain voltage
  (-5V = -24dB, 0V = unity, +5V = +24dB, default 0).
- **inputGain** — gain before the compressor (-5V = -24dB, 0V = unity,
  5V = +24dB). Raising input gain drives more signal into the compressor.
- **outputGain** — gain after compression (-5V = -24dB, 0V = unity,
  5V = +24dB). Trims the final output level.
- **mix** — dry/wet blend (0 = fully dry, 5 = fully wet, default 5.0).
  The dry signal is the original input before any gain staging.

```js
// simple bus compressor
$comp($saw('c2'), { threshold: 2.5, ratio: 4, attack: 0.01, release: 0.1 })
```

```js
// side-chain ducking — a kick envelope ducks a sustained pad
$comp($saw('c3'), {
  sidechain: $perc($clock.beatTrigger, { decay: 0.2 }),
  threshold: 1.0, ratio: 8, attack: 0.005, release: 0.2,
})
```

```js
// multiband compression using $xover + $comp
let bands = $xover($saw('c2'), { lowMidFreq: '200hz', midHighFreq: '2000hz' })
let low  = $comp(bands.low,  { threshold: 2.5, ratio: 4 })
let mid  = $comp(bands.mid,  { threshold: 3,   ratio: 3 })
let high = $comp(bands.high, { threshold: 2,   ratio: 6 })
$mix([low, mid, high]).out()
```

name: $xover
documentation:
EXPERIMENTAL

Three-band crossover / band splitter.

Splits an input signal into three frequency bands (low, mid, high).
The default `sample` output passes the input through unchanged,
so the module is a no-op unless you explicitly tap the
`.low`, `.mid`, or `.high` outputs.

Two crossover frequencies define the band boundaries:
- **lowMidFreq** — boundary between the low and mid bands (V/Oct, default ~200 Hz).
- **midHighFreq** — boundary between the mid and high bands (V/Oct, default ~2000 Hz).

```js
// Split into 3 bands and process each independently
let bands = $xover($saw('c2'), { lowMidFreq: '200hz', midHighFreq: '2000hz' })
let low  = $comp(bands.low,  { threshold: 2.5, ratio: 4 })
let mid  = $comp(bands.mid,  { threshold: 3,   ratio: 3 })
let high = $comp(bands.high, { threshold: 2,   ratio: 6 })
$mix([low, mid, high]).out()
```

documentation:
Adds bright, granular quantization noise to a signal.

The signal is snapped to a coarse voltage grid (`step`), dithered so the
result is broadband noise instead of a tonal buzz, then the quantized value
is differentiated and scaled by `amount` and summed back onto the dry signal.
Because the grit is the signal's own (dithered) quantization residual, it
tracks the signal's level and motion — feed it a slow LFO for a fizz that
swells with the modulator, or audio for a crunchy digital edge.

## Example

```js
$quantNoise($sine('c'), 2).out() // grainy, fizzy sine
```

dither.description: dither depth: 0 a tonal staircase buzz that tracks the signal, 5 broadband noise

step.description: size of the voltage grid the signal snaps to, in volts; bigger steps give coarser grit

name: $unstable.reverb
documentation:
Stereo Feedback Delay Network reverb.

The eight modulated delay lines are split into a left and a right
sub-network. Even input channels feed the left half, odd channels the right,
so the wet field tracks the dry stereo image; a `width` control sets how
strongly the two halves cross-couple, from held-apart to collapsed to mono.
Each line has a decay gain tuned so the network reaches −60 dB at the
requested `decay`, plus a one-pole damping filter for a natural
high-frequency rolloff. Per-channel predelay and diffusion sit ahead of the
network. Output is always 100% wet — use `.send()` or `$mix` for a dry/wet

name: $unstable.reverb2
documentation:
Stereo Jot-style Feedback Delay Network reverb with a scattering matrix.

The eight modulated delay lines split into a left and a right sub-network,
each recirculating through its own paraunitary scattering matrix — a
Hadamard mix, short per-line delays, then a Householder mix — so energy
diffuses densely without a fixed metallic structure. Even input channels
feed the left half, odd the right, so the wet field tracks the dry stereo
image; a `width` control sets how strongly the halves cross-couple. Each
line's feedback runs through a first-order absorption filter that sets a
two-band decay time (`decay` for the low band, `damping` for how much faster
the high band decays), and a matching tonal-correction shelf flattens the
output timbre. Per-channel predelay and diffusion sit ahead of the network.
Output is always 100% wet — use `.send()` or `$mix` for a dry/wet blend.

```js
$unstable.reverb2($saw('c3')).out()
$unstable.reverb2($saw('c3'), { decay: 3, damping: 2, size: 2 }).out()
$unstable.reverb2($saw('c3'), { decay: 4, width: 4, modulation: 3 }).out()
```

name: $granular
documentation:
Granular processor from Mutable Instruments Beads: it records `input` and
plays it back as grains, starting one on each rising edge at `trigger`.

Each grain takes `time`, `size`, `shape`, `freq` and `spread` when it
starts, so for grain-to-grain variation modulate them with something
sampled on the same trigger, such as `$sah`. Set `rootFreq` to the
pitch of the input and `freq` plays notes. `freeze` holds the recording
so the grains keep replaying it.

Each input channel gets its own voice. `output` is a stereo mix of every
voice, and `voices` gives each voice its own channel. Follow it with
`$wowFlutter` and `$reverb` for the rest of Beads' sound.

```js
const grains = $pulse('8hz')
$granular($saw('a3'), grains, {
  time: $sah($noise('white').range(0, 2), grains),
  freq: $cycle($p('[c4, e4, g4] [b3, d4, g4]')),
  rootFreq: 'a3',
  width: 4,
  spread: 2,
  mix: 4,
}).out()
```

name: $clockedDelay
documentation:
Tempo-synced delay from Mutable Instruments Beads' delay mode. Its repeats
come from feedback inside the module, so it needs no feedback loop in the
patch.

The delay time is `bars` of the playhead, which follows the transport,
times a multiplier set by `time`. When the time or the tempo changes, the
old repeats crossfade into the new ones at an unchanged pitch.
`shape` windows each repeat with an envelope one delay time long, locked
to the playhead, so the repeats come back as rhythmic slices;
`grooveAmount` swings the windows with the global groove. `freq`
shifts their pitch against `rootFreq`, and `tone` filters them. While
`freeze` is high the delay stops recording and loops slices of what it
holds, one base delay time long; `time` then picks the slice.

Each input channel gets its own delay. Follow it with `$wowFlutter` and
`$reverb` for the rest of Beads' sound.

```js
const pluck = $saw('c3').amplitude($perc($clock.beatTrigger, { decay: 0.1 }))
$clockedDelay(pluck, { bars: 3 / 16, feedback: 3 }).out()
```

name: $noise
documentation:
Polyphonic noise generator with selectable color and clock rate.

Spectral colors:
- **white**: equal energy across all frequencies (bright, hissy)
- **pink**: equal energy per octave (warm, balanced — good for "ocean" textures)
- **brown**: steep low-frequency emphasis (deep, rumbling)
- **blue** / **violet**: high-frequency emphasis (+3 / +6 dB/octave), for hats and air

Distributions and digital noise:
- **binary**: only −5V or +5V — at the same peak it is louder than white
- **gaussian**: values cluster near 0V with occasional large excursions
- **lfsr** / **lfsrShort**: NES-style shift-register noise; lfsr repeats every 32767 ticks,
  lfsrShort every 93, which sounds pitched and metallic — its `rate` sets that pitch

Impulse and switching noise:
- **velvet**: exactly one ±5V trigger per tick, at a random moment within it, resting at 0V
- **telegraph**: ±5V that flips at random moments, on average `rate` times per second
- **dust**: rests at −5V with +5V triggers, on average `rate` per second; like
  Mutable Instruments Beads' random grain triggers, each gap is 0.12–2.36× the average, so
  triggers are loosely irregular with no long silences

Velvet and dust triggers last the standard trigger length (about 0.33 ms),
shortened toward a single sample when the next trigger comes sooner, so
every trigger stays distinct.

`rate` clocks the generator: the color is computed at that rate, so slow
rates give random CV (a slow brown is a drunk walk) and audio rates give
lo-fi, band-limited noise. `interp` shapes the output between ticks;
`linear` and `smooth` turn any color into a smooth random LFO. Unconnected,
the generator draws a new value every sample, telegraph flips on half of all
samples, and dust triggers every two samples on average.

The `channels` parameter sets how many independent channels are generated;
each channel runs its own RNG seeded distinctly, so every channel is a
different random sequence.

Output range is **±5V**.

## Example

```js
$noise("pink").out()
$noise("white", { channels: 4 }).out()
$noise("lfsrShort", { rate: "c3" }).out()
$sine($noise("brown", { rate: $hz(4), interp: "smooth" })).out()
```

interp.description: how the output moves between draws while `rate` is patched

documentation:
Lowpass filter that attenuates frequencies above the cutoff point.

Use it to tame bright timbres, create bass-heavy sounds, or build classic
subtractive synth patches. Sweeping the cutoff with an envelope or LFO

- **resonance** — boosts frequencies near the cutoff (0–5). High values
  produce a ringing peak, but the filter never self-oscillates; use
  `$jup6f` for a filter that does.

```js
// subtractive bass: saw through a lowpass with envelope on cutoff
let env = $adsr($pPulse($clock[0]), { attack: 0.01, decay: 0.3, sustain: 1, release: 0.4 })
$lpf($saw('c2'), env.range('200hz', '2000hz'))
```

name: $apf
documentation:
Stacked allpass filter: 1 to 50 two-pole stages, with resonance and
feedback. Smears transients into chirps around the cutoff; mixed with the
dry signal, it notches like a phaser.

- **cutoff** — V/Oct, the frequency delayed most.
- **stages** — 1–50. More stages, longer smear. A fractional count fades
  the next stage in smoothly.
- **resonance** — 0–5. Makes the smear ring at the cutoff's pitch.
- **feedback** — −5 to 5. Repeats the smear; rings get longer toward ±5,
  where they never fade. Up to ±6 the filter self-oscillates. Negative
  values flip the sign of every other repeat.
- **fadeStep** — 0–49. Above 0, `stages` crossfades between chains this
  many stages apart instead, giving notches.

```js
// smear a click on every beat into a chirp around C3
$pPulse($clock[0]).$.apf('c3', { stages: 50 }).out()
// ringing, pitched smear with repeats
$pPulse($clock[0]).$.apf('g3', { stages: 32, resonance: 3, feedback: 3 }).out()
// self-oscillating: no input, just the loop
$apf(0, 'c3', { stages: 20, resonance: 2, feedback: 5.5 }).out()
// notches: crossfading between chains 8 stages apart
$noise('white').$.apf('c4', { stages: $sine('0.05hz').range(9, 25), resonance: 2, fadeStep: 8 }).out()
// four-stage phaser: swept allpass mixed equally with the dry saw
$saw('c2').$m.apf(2.5, $sine('0.2hz').range(-1, 3), { stages: 4, resonance: 2, feedback: 3 }).out()
```

name: $jup6f
documentation:
Jupiter-6–style multimode ladder filter.

Models the IR3109 4-pole OTA cascade found in the Roland Jupiter-6.
Each stage applies `tanh` saturation for the warm, harmonically rich

- **resonance** — feedback amount (0–5). Above ~4 the filter self-oscillates,
  producing a clean sine at the cutoff frequency.


name: $lpg
documentation:
Vactrol low pass gate modeled on the one built into Mutable Instruments Plaits.

The gate is a filter and VCA driven together by a simulated vactrol: as it
opens, the signal gets both louder and brighter, and it closes with the
slow, non-linear tail that gives plucked and struck sounds their bounce.

- **trigger** — each rising edge pings the vactrol fully open, then it
  decays back to **level**.
- **level** — the floor the vactrol rests at, 0–5 V on Plaits' compressing
  curve: about 0.9 V opens it halfway, 2.5 V about 80%, 5 V fully. With no
  trigger it works as a CV-controlled gate; with a trigger, each ping
  swings the gate from the floor to fully open and back.
- **color** — low values close the filter as the gate closes (mellow,
  woody); high values let highs through, approaching a plain VCA.
- **decay** — length of the vactrol's release.

With neither **trigger** nor **level** patched the gate is bypassed and
the input passes through unchanged; patching or unpatching them
crossfades over 5 ms.

```js
// plucked saw pinged on every beat
$lpg($saw('c3'), $clock.beatTrigger, { color: 1.5, decay: 2 }).out()
```

name: $multimode
documentation:
Mutable Instruments Blades–style multimode filter with drive and wavefolder.

A circuit model of one channel of Blades: a 2164 VCA state-variable filter
that morphs continuously from lowpass through bandpass to highpass, preceded
by a drive VCA into a zener soft clipper and a two-stage diode wavefolder.
The signal path is DC-coupled, so it can process CVs too.

- **cutoff** — V/Oct. Tracks exactly at low cutoffs and runs progressively
  flat in the top octaves (−15 cents at 1 kHz, about half a semitone at
  5 kHz), topping out near 21 kHz, as the circuit does. Responds at audio
  rate, so an oscillator patched in gives exponential FM.
- **resonance** — 0–5. Self-oscillates above ~4.3; the bandpass is then
  held near ±4 V by the soft knee of the integrator's zeners. With no input,
  `mode` shifts the phase of the sine.
- **mode** — 0 lowpass, 2.5 bandpass, 5 highpass; values between crossfade.
- **drive** — input gain ahead of everything else: 0 is unity, 5 is about
  +18 dB. The zeners' soft knee already rounds a ±5 V input at 0.
- **fold** — 0 soft clipping only, 5 the two-stage wavefolder.
- **highRes** — on by default. Off runs the circuit at the engine rate for
  less CPU, with more aliasing from hot drive, folding and self-oscillation,
  and a highpass that attenuates more below the cutoff once the cutoff is
  above ~8 kHz (about 2 dB more at 15 kHz).

Passband gain in lowpass mode is about +2.8 dB at unity drive, rolling off
above ~20 kHz at the output amp, whose zeners compress the output softly
above about 6 V.

```js
// resonant sweep that morphs from lowpass to highpass
$multimode($saw('c2'), $sine('0.1hz').range(-1, 2), 3.8, $sine('0.07hz').range(0, 5)).out()
// wavefolded sine through a gentle lowpass
$multimode($sine('c3'), 'c6', 1, 0, { drive: 3, fold: 3 }).out()
// no input: a self-oscillating sine at A3
$multimode(0, 'a3', 5).out()
// without oversampling, for less CPU
$multimode($saw('c2'), 'c5', 2, 0, { highRes: false }).out()
```

name: $eq
documentation:
Parametric EQ: shape the tone of a sound with up to 8 bands.

Each band in **sections** has a **type**:

- `'peak'` (default): boost or cut around a frequency.
- `'lowShelf'` / `'highShelf'`: boost or cut everything below / above a
  frequency.
- `'lowpass'` / `'highpass'`: remove everything above / below a frequency.
- `'notch'`: remove a narrow band around a frequency.

and sets:

- **freq**: where the band sits, like `'1000hz'` or `'c4'`.
- **gain**: how much to boost or cut, in dB (-24 to 24). Peaks and shelves
  only.
- **q**: how narrow the band is (0.1 to 20, default 0.707). On shelves and
  lowpass/highpass, values above 0.707 add a resonant bump at the
  frequency; on shelves, lower values make a gentler slope.

Any of them can be modulated. With no sections, the sound passes through
unchanged.

To EQ channels differently, give **sections** one list of bands per
channel, like one for left and one for right.

**adaptiveQ** makes peaks narrower the more you boost or cut them, like
many classic analog EQs.

**ui: true** shows an editor under the call. Drag a band's dot to move it,
scroll over it or drag its handles to change q, and double-click to add a
band. Changes play right away and are written into your code. Hold
Ctrl/Cmd to change only the code, and right-click a control to reset it.

```js
// Warm up the lows, sweep a dip through the mids, clear out rumble
$eq($saw('c2'), {
  sections: [
    { type: 'lowShelf', freq: '150hz', gain: 3 },
    { type: 'peak', freq: $sine('0.5hz').range('400hz', '2000hz'), gain: -6, q: 2 },
    { type: 'highpass', freq: '40hz' },
  ],
  adaptiveQ: true,
})

// A darker left channel, a brighter right one
$eq($saw(['c2', 'g2']), {
  sections: [
    [{ type: 'highShelf', freq: '3000hz', gain: -6 }],
    [{ type: 'highShelf', freq: '3000hz', gain: 4 }],
  ],
})

// Start empty and build the EQ in the editor
$eq($saw('c2'), { ui: true })
```

name: $adsr
documentation:
An Attack-Decay-Sustain-Release envelope generator.

Generates a control voltage envelope driven by a **gate** input.
When the gate goes high (>1V) the envelope enters the attack phase;
when the gate goes low it enters release.

- **attack** / **decay** / **release** — time in seconds
- **sustain** — level in volts (0–5V). Defaults to 5V, but if **decay** is set
  without **sustain**, sustain defaults to 0V for a plucky attack-decay shape.
- **curve** — ramp shape from -5 to 5. 0 is linear; +5 gives a logarithmic
  attack and exponential decay/release; -5 is the inverse.
  Defaults to 5.
- **retrigger** — a rising edge restarts the attack from the current level
  (no jump). Defaults to the gate input. Set **resetOnRetrig** to true to
  instead snap back to the start of the attack on every retrigger.

Output range is **0–5V**.

## Example

```js
const env = $adsr($pPulse($clock[0]), { attack: 0.01, decay: 0.2, sustain: 3, release: 0.5 })
$sine('c4').amplitude(env).out()
```

name: $chord
documentation:
Outputs the notes of a scale or chord as a polyphonic V/Oct signal, one
channel per note in ascending pitch.

The spec is a root note (optional octave, default 4) followed by a scale in
`()` or a chord in `[]`:

| Form | Example | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| `root(scale)` | `"C(major)"`, `"D3(dorian)"` | Named scale, one octave |
| `root(intervals)` | `"C(0 3 7 10)"` | Semitones from the root, reduced to one octave |
| `root(tuning)` | `"C(just)"`, `"A(pythag)"` | All 12 steps in a non-equal tuning |
| `root[chord]` | `"C[maj7]"`, `"F#2[m9]"` | Chord shorthand; extensions keep their register |
| `root[intervals]` | `"C[0 7 16]"` | Custom voicing; intervals keep their register |
| `root[tuning chord]` | `"C[just maj]"` | Tuning prefix (`just`, `pythag`, `pythagorean`) |
| `root[chord invN]` | `"C[maj7 inv1]"` | Raises the lowest N notes an octave |
| `chromatic` | `"chromatic"` | All 12 semitones from C4 |

Scale names: major/maj/ionian/M, minor/min/aeolian/m, dorian, phrygian,
lydian, mixolydian, locrian, harmonic minor, melodic minor, pentatonic
major/minor, blues, whole tone, chromatic.

Chord names (case-sensitive): maj/M/major, min/m/minor, dim/°, aug/+,
sus2, sus4/sus, 5, 6, m6, 69, 7/dom7, maj7/M7/Δ/Δ7, m7/min7, mMaj7/mM7,
dim7/°7, m7b5/ø/ø7, aug7/7#5/+7, maj7#5, 7sus4, 7sus2, 7b5, 9, maj9, m9,
11, maj11, m11, 13, maj13, m13, 7b9, 7#9, 7#11, add9/add2, madd9,
add11/add4.

```js
// a C major 7th chord on four saw voices
$saw($chord("C3[maj7]")).out()
```


documentation:
Sends each trigger to heads or tails at random.

Each trigger on **input** flips a weighted coin, and **probability** sets
the chance of heads. The module itself is the heads output; `.tails`
carries the rest. Gates keep their length, and each channel flips on its
own.

or use both outputs to split one stream between two sounds.

```js

const flip = $coinFlip($clock.beatTrigger, 3.75)
$tr808.kick(flip).out()
```

name: $scan
documentation:
Steps a counter by `distance` on each trigger, wrapping it within 0 to
`length`.

A step past `length` wraps around by the overshoot, as many times as it
takes, and so does a step below 0. With `snapOnWrap`, a step past
`length` lands on 0 and a step below 0 lands on `length`. A counter
exactly at `length` stays there. `reset` sets the counter to 0, and wins
over a trigger in the same sample. Lengths are read at each trigger, so a
shorter `length` takes effect on the next step.

```js

```

documentation:
Applies a power curve to a signal, normalised at ±5 V.

Formula: `sign(x) × 5 × (|x| / 5) ^ exp`

- **exp > 1** — pushes midrange toward zero (audio taper)
- **0 < exp < 1** — pushes midrange toward ±5 V
- **exp = 0** — step function (any nonzero → ±5 V)

```js
$curve($sine('1hz'), 2)   // quadratic curve
$curve($saw('c3'), 3)     // cubic curve (audio taper)
```

Applies a wandering random variation to a signal.

**shift** mode adds an offset of up to ±**amount**, scaled to the width of

shifts the same way, then clamps to the range. **blend** mode moves toward a

**bias** makes the variation lean upward (+)
or downward (−); ±5 makes it one-sided. **sparse** draws a random depth per
value: low amounts mostly stay near the input with rare big jumps, high
amounts mostly jump. **speed** runs from frozen at 0 to a

between rising edges.

from a ranged signal's range.

name: $hold
documentation:
Stretches a trigger into a fixed-length gate.

A rising edge on the input opens the output at 5V for `time` seconds,
regardless of when the input falls; the output closes after `time` even if
the input is still high. A rising edge while the output is high
retriggers it: the output drops low for a brief retrigger gap, so
downstream envelopes see a new rising edge, and the gate closes `time`
after the new edge.

## Example

```js
// stretch short clock pulses into 100 ms gates
const env = $adsr($hold($clock.beatTrigger, 0.1))
$sine('c4').amplitude(env).out()
```

name: $slew
documentation:
Slew limiter that smooths abrupt voltage changes.

Separate **rise** and **fall** times control how quickly the output can
increase or decrease. Times are specified in **seconds per volt** — the
time the output takes to slew by 1 V. For example, a rise time of `0.1`
means the output climbs 1 V in 0.1 s; a 5 V gate signal would therefore
take 0.5 s to reach full height.

Use `$slew` to add portamento to pitch signals, smooth noisy control
voltages, or create envelope-like shapes from gate signals.

```js
// portamento: glide between notes (0.1 s per volt of pitch change)
$sine($slew($cycle($p('c3 e3 g3')), { rise: 0.1, fall: 0.1 }))
```

name: $math
documentation:
Evaluates a math expression every sample, giving you arbitrary control
voltage transformations.

Write an expression string using `x`, `y`, `z` as input variables.
The built-in variable `t` (time in seconds) is also available.

The inputs are polyphonic: the module is as wide as its widest input, the
expression is evaluated once per channel, and narrower inputs cycle. A
non-finite result (e.g. `0/0`) is emitted as 0.

**Functions:** `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`,
`sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `asinh`, `acosh`, `atanh`,
`log(base?, val)`, `abs`, `sign`, `int`, `ceil`, `floor`,
`round(modulus?, val)`, `min(val, ...)`, `max(val, ...)`,
`e()`, `pi()`, `vToHz(volts)`, `hzToV(hz)`

**Operators** (highest to lowest precedence):
`^`, `%`, `/`, `*`, `-`, `+`,
`== != < <= >= >`,
`&& and`, `|| or`

```js
// crossfade between two oscillators

```

name: $motionFollower
documentation:
Turns controller movement into a level, like bowing a string: moving the
input in either direction swells the output, holding it still lets it fade.

The input's speed (volts per second, direction ignored) is averaged over
**smooth** seconds, then followed with separate **attack** and **release**
times. **gain** converts speed to volts and a soft clip keeps the output
below **ceiling**.

**pos** and **neg** are the same level driven only by rising or only by
falling input, so pushing and releasing a controller can steer different
destinations. Both are positive voltages.

Stepped controllers such as 7-bit MIDI CC jump in small increments, so
their raw speed is a train of spikes; a **smooth** time several times longer
than the gap between updates averages them into a steady level.

```js
// a slowly swinging LFO bows a filter open on every sweep
$lpf($saw('c3'), $motionFollower($sine('0.5hz'), { release: 0.5 }).range('c3', 'c7')).out()
```

name: $sah
documentation:
Captures and holds a voltage on each trigger.

When **trigger** receives a rising edge, the current value of **input**
is sampled and held at the output until the next trigger. Classic
use: sample random noise to generate stepped random melodies.

```js
// stepped random melody
$sine(
 $quantizer(
   $sah($noise('white').range(0, 1), $pulse('2hz')),
   'c(maj)',
 ),
)
```

trigger.description: rising edge captures the current input value

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: the voltage captured at the last trigger

signalParams.name: input
signalParams.description: signal to sample

signalParams.name: trigger
signalParams.description: rising edge captures the current input value

name: $tah
documentation:
Follows the input while the gate is low, and holds the value when the
gate goes high.

The complement of Sample and Hold: the output continuously tracks
**input** until **gate** rises, then freezes until the gate falls again.

```js
// hold a slow sine value while the gate is high
$tah($sine('2hz'), $pulse('2hz'))
```

gate.description: output follows the input while low and holds its last value while high

signalParams.name: input
signalParams.description: signal to track

signalParams.name: gate
signalParams.description: output follows the input while low and holds its last value while high

name: $perc
documentation:
Simple envelope for percussive sounds.

A rising edge on **trigger** starts the envelope at 5 V, which then
decays exponentially to 0 V over the **decay** time. Perfect for
hi-hats, kicks, and other transient sounds.

Output range is **0–5 V**.

```js
// short percussive hit
$noise("white").amplitude($perc($clock.beatTrigger, { decay: 0.1 })).out()
```

decay.description: how long the envelope takes to die away, in seconds

trigger.description: rising edge restarts the envelope from its current level

signalParams.name: trigger
signalParams.description: rising edge restarts the envelope from its current level

signalParams.name: decay
signalParams.description: how long the envelope takes to die away, in seconds

name: $quantizer
documentation:
Snaps a V/Oct signal to the nearest note of a scale.

**scale** is a polyphonic signal: each channel is one V/Oct note, and the
output snaps to the nearest of those notes in any octave. Feed it from
`$chord`, a `$cycle`, or `$midiCV` — or pass a spec string such as
`"C(major)"` or `"C[maj7]"`, which is shorthand for `$chord(spec)` (see
`$chord` for the full grammar). Without a scale, the output snaps to
semitones.

**gate** selects which scale notes are active: scale channel N is used only
while gate channel N is high. While every gate channel is low, the output
holds its last note.

A **trig** pulse fires whenever the quantized note changes, useful for
re-triggering envelopes.

```js
// quantize a slow sine to C major
$sine($quantizer($sine("0.1hz").range(0, 3), "C(major)")).out()
```

```js
// quantize to whichever MIDI keys are held; holds when all are released
const midi = $midiCV({ channels: 4 })
$sine($quantizer($sine("0.1hz").range(-1, 1), midi, { gate: midi.gate })).out()
```

gate.description: turns notes of the scale on and off: scale channel N is used only while gate channel N is high; with every gate low the output holds

offset.description: transposition added to the pitch before it snaps

scale.description: notes to snap to, one pitch per channel in any octave, or a spec like "C(major)" or "C[maj7]"; snaps to semitones when left out

outputs.name: trig
outputs.description: a short trigger each time the snapped note changes

signalParams.description: transposition added to the pitch before it snaps

name: $scaleAndShift
documentation:
Scales and offsets a signal — the classic attenuverter + DC offset.

- **scale** — gain factor (0–10 V; 5 V = unity, 0 V = silence,
  values above 5 V amplify, negative values invert).
- **shift** — DC offset added after scaling (in volts).

```js
// invert a slow sine and shift it into 0–5 V range
$scaleAndShift($sine('1hz'), -2.5, 2.5)
```

name: _smoothControl
documentation:
A UI-driven constant: the editor sets `value` through the single-module
update path, and the output ramps linearly to it over [`RAMP_SECONDS`] so
a drag's stepped values move without zipper noise. A freshly built control
starts at its value; one that replaces another continues from the old
output. Backs `$slider`, the out gain/pan faders, and the mute/solo gate.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: the value, ramping smoothly to each new setting

name: $spread
documentation:
Produces a multi-channel output by linearly interpolating between a
minimum and maximum value, with an optional bias to skew the
distribution.

Each output channel gets an evenly spaced value between **min** and
**max**. The **bias** control reshapes the distribution: positive
values push channels toward **max**, negative values toward **min**.

| count | behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| 1     | single value between min and max, positioned by bias |
| 2     | channel 0 = min, channel 1 = max (with bias = 0) |
| N     | N evenly spaced values from min to max (with bias = 0) |

```js
// spread 4 oscillators across a frequency range
$sine($spread(0, 5, 4))

// 8 channels biased toward the minimum
$spread(0, 5, 8, { bias: -3 })
```

bias.description: bunches the channels toward max (positive) or min (negative); 0 spaces them evenly

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: one value per channel, from min to max

signalParams.name: min
signalParams.description: value of the first channel

signalParams.name: max
signalParams.description: value of the last channel

signalParams.name: bias
signalParams.description: bunches the channels toward max (positive) or min (negative); 0 spaces them evenly

name: $unison
documentation:
Expands each input channel into multiple detuned copies for unison effects.

Takes a signal (typically V/Oct pitch) and multiplies channels by the
unison count, applying symmetric detuning controlled by the spread parameter.

- **count** — number of detuned copies per input channel (1–64)
- **spread** — detune amount with exponential curve (0–10V → 0–1 octave V/Oct)

Output channels = `max(input_channels, spread_channels) × count`, clamped to
64. **input** and **spread** cycle against each other, so a spread wider than
the input repeats the input across the extra channels, and vice versa.

Voices are interleaved: each voice is a full copy of the input channels, so a
3-channel input with count 3 outputs channels `1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3`. When the
64-channel cap truncates, the highest voices are the ones dropped.

## Example

```js
// 7-voice unison saw with moderate spread
$saw($unison('c4', 7, 5)).out()

// With modulated spread
$saw($unison($midiCV(), 5, $sine('0.2hz'))).out()
```

count.description: number of detuned copies per input channel

input.description: pitch to fan out into detuned copies

spread.description: detune width, finer near 0: 0 none, 10 puts the outer copies an octave above and below

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: the detuned copies, each a full set of the input channels

signalParams.name: input
signalParams.description: pitch to fan out into detuned copies

signalParams.name: spread
signalParams.description: detune width, finer near 0: 0 none, 10 puts the outer copies an octave above and below

name: _videoTap
documentation:
Publishes its input to the video renderer, which polls the latest value
and the recent samples of each tap slot. The DSL inserts one per audio
signal a `$v` input reads.

input.description: signal published to the video renderer

slot.description: tap slot the renderer reads it from

signalParams.name: input
signalParams.description: signal published to the video renderer

name: $wrap
documentation:
Folds a signal into a range by wrapping values that exceed the boundaries
back from the opposite side — like a phase accumulator.

Both **min** and **max** accept polyphonic signals. If **max** < **min**
the bounds are swapped automatically.

Set **octave** to `true` to shift by whole integers instead, preserving the
fractional part (pitch class in V/Oct signals). Always exact when
`max − min ≥ 1`; makes the closest-octave attempt otherwise.

```js
// wrap a saw into 0–5 V
$wrap($saw('c3'), 0, 5)
// keep pitch class, clamp to octave range 0–2 V
$wrap($cycle($p('c2 c5 c3')), 0, 2, { octave: true })
```

min.description: bottom of the range; swaps with max when above it

octave.description: shift by whole volts (octaves) instead, keeping the note and moving only its octave

signalParams.name: input
signalParams.description: signal to wrap

signalParams.name: min
signalParams.description: bottom of the range; swaps with max when above it

signalParams.name: max
signalParams.description: top of the range

name: $cycle
documentation:
Pattern sequencer using mini-notation strings.

Write rhythmic and melodic patterns using a compact text syntax ported
from TidalCycles/Strudel. The pattern loops each **cycle** and supports
polyphony — overlapping notes are automatically allocated to separate
output channels.

## Cycles

A **cycle** is one full traversal of the pattern. The playhead position
determines timing: its integer part selects the current cycle number and
the fractional part selects the position within that cycle. Space-separated
values divide the cycle into equal time slots.

## Values

| Syntax | Meaning | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| Note name | Pitch (octave defaults to 3) | `'c4'`, `'a#3'`, `'db5'` |
| Bare number | MIDI note number | `60`, `72` |
| `Xhz` | Frequency | `'440hz'` |
| `Xv` | Explicit voltage | `'0v'`, `'1v'`, `'-0.5v'` |
| `~` | Rest (gate low, no change in CV) | `'c4 ~ e4 ~'` |

Bare numbers are MIDI note numbers (A0 = MIDI 33 = 0 V).

## Grouping

- **`[a b c]`** — fast subsequence: subdivides the parent time slot so all
  elements play within it.
- **`<a b c>`** — slow / alternating: plays one element per cycle,
  advancing each time the pattern loops.

```js
$cycle($p("c4 [d4 e4]"))   // c4 for half the cycle, d4 & e4 share the other half
$cycle($p("<c4 g4> e4"))   // cycle 1: c4 e4, cycle 2: g4 e4, …
```

## Stacks

**`a b, c d`** — comma-separated patterns play **simultaneously** (layered).
Each sub-pattern has its own independent timing.

```js
$cycle($p("c4 e4, g4 b4"))   // two patterns layered on top of each other
$cycle($p("c4 d4 e4, g3"))   // three-note melody over a pedal tone
```

## Random choice

**`a|b|c`** — randomly selects one option each time the slot is reached.

```js
$cycle($p("c4|d4|e4 g4"))  // first slot is a random pick each cycle
```

## Nesting

Grouping, stacks, and random choice nest arbitrarily:

```js
$cycle($p("<c4 [d4 e4]> [f4|g4 a4]"))  // slow + fast + random combined
$cycle($p("[c4 e4, g4] a4"))           // stack inside a fast subsequence
```

## Per-element modifiers

Modifiers attach directly to an element (no spaces). Multiple modifiers
can be chained in any order.

| Modifier | Syntax | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Weight | `@n` | Relative duration within a sequence (default 1). `c4@2 e4` gives c4 twice the time. |
| Speed up | `*n` | Repeat/subdivide `n` times within the slot. `c4*3` plays c4 three times. |
| Slow down | `/n` | Stretch over `n` cycles. `c4/2` plays every other cycle. |
| Replicate | `!n` | Duplicate the element `n` times (default 2). `c4!3` is equivalent to `c4 c4 c4`. |
| Degrade | `?` or `?n` | Randomly drop the element. `c4?` drops ~50 % of the time; `c4?0.8` drops 80 %. |
| Euclidean | `(k,n)` or `(k,n,offset)` | Distribute `k` pulses over `n` steps using the Bjorklund algorithm. Optional `offset` rotates the pattern. |

```js
$cycle($p("c4*2 e4 g4"))        // c4 plays twice in its slot
$cycle($p("c4@3 e4 g4"))        // c4 gets 3/5 of the cycle, e4 and g4 get 1/5 each
$cycle($p("c4? e4 g4"))         // c4 randomly drops out ~50 % of the time
$cycle($p("c4(3,8) e4"))        // Euclidean: 3 hits spread over 8 steps
$cycle($p("[c4 d4 e4 f4](3,8)")) // Euclidean applied to a subpattern
```

Modifier operands can also be subpatterns: `c4*[2 3]` alternates between
doubling and tripling each slot.

## Outputs

- **cv** — V/Oct pitch (C4 = 0 V).
- **gate** — 5 V while a note is active, 0 V otherwise.
- **trig** — single-sample 5 V pulse at each note onset.
- **velocity** — groove velocity (0–5 V) sampled at each note onset.

## Groove

By default notes start on the global groove set with `$setGroove`, and
`velocity` reports that groove's step velocity. The groove moves when each
note starts; every note keeps its written length. Pass a `$groove` as
`groove` (with its `velocity`) to use a different groove, or `groove: 0` to
play straight.

```js
$setGroove($swing(0.6))
const hats = $cycle($p('c5*8'))
const bass = $cycle($p('c2*4'), { groove: 0 })
$sine(hats).amp($adsr(hats.gate)).amp(hats.velocity).out()
$sine(bass).amp($adsr(bass.gate)).out()
```

Atomic value types produced by the `$p()` DSL parser.

The reduced set from strudel's krill grammar: `Number` covers bare

covers pitched letter-octave atoms (`c4`, `d#3`, `eb5`), and `Truthy`
covers the `x` structure marker. Every other atom form (`m60` midi
shorthand, sample-name identifiers, `2v` voltage, module references,
quoted strings) has been removed from the grammar and is not
representable here.

name: $drumMap
documentation:
Topographic drum sequencer: a port of Mutable Instruments Grids.

Three trigger streams — bass drum, snare and hi-hat — are read from a
5×5 map of drum patterns. **x** and **y** (0–5 V) move smoothly through
the map, interpolating between neighbouring patterns. Each part's
**density** sets how many of its possible hits play, from silence at 0 V
to every hit at 5 V. **chaos** adds random variation, re-rolled each
cycle. Strong hits also fire the matching accent output.

One cycle of the **playhead** plays the 32-step pattern once.

Steps follow the global groove set with `$setGroove`, and the groove's
step **velocity** decides how readily each hit accents: at full velocity
accents are as in Grids, and quieter steps accent only their strongest
hits. Pass a `$groove` as `groove` (with its `velocity`) to use a
different groove, or `groove: 0` to play straight.

```js
const drums = $drumMap({ x: 1, y: 3, chaos: 0.5 })
// the bass drum is the default output
$sine('c1').amplitude($perc(drums, { decay: 0.3 })).out()
$noise('white').amplitude($perc(drums.hh, { decay: 0.05 })).out()
```

bdDensity.description: how many bass drum hits play: none at 0, all at 5

chaos.description: random variation of the pattern, re-rolled each cycle

groove.description: groove shift of each step, in cycles; follows the global groove by default, and is 0 when `playhead` is set without it

hhDensity.description: how many hi-hat hits play: none at 0, all at 5

playhead.description: playhead position in cycles; one cycle plays the 32-step pattern once; follows the global clock by default

resolution.description: steps per cycle; 32 adds ghost notes

sdDensity.description: how many snare drum hits play: none at 0, all at 5

velocity.description: how readily each step accents: lower accents less, 0 never; follows the global groove by default, and is full when `playhead` or `groove` is set without it

x.description: horizontal position in the map of drum patterns

y.description: vertical position in the map of drum patterns

oneOf.description: 16 steps per cycle, playing the map's even steps (Grids at 4 ppqn)
all 32 steps per cycle, including the map's ghost notes (Grids at 8 or 24 ppqn)

name: $groove
documentation:
Groove a playhead with a timing and velocity template.

The template moves each grid step by its timing offset. A `$cycle` given
this module's offset starts grid-aligned notes at the shifted times, slides
notes between grid steps proportionally, and keeps every note's length.
Every `$cycle` follows the global groove (see `$setGroove`) by default;
pass this module's offset and velocity to give one its own groove.

Timing offsets are in grid steps: with `grid: 16`, an offset of `0.2` delays
that sixteenth by a fifth of a sixteenth. The template repeats every
`timing.length` steps.

```js
const g = $groove({ timing: [0, 0.3], velocity: [1, 0.6] })
const seq = $cycle($p('c4*8'), { groove: g, velocity: g.velocity })
$sine(seq).amp($adsr(seq.gate)).amp(seq.velocity).out()
```

playhead.description: straight playhead to groove, in cycles; follows the global clock (without its groove) by default

template.description: timing offsets, velocities and step grid of the groove

GrooveTemplate.description: Groove template: per-step timing offsets and velocities over a grid.

amount.description: timing strength: scales every offset (0 = straight, 1 = as written)

grid.description: grid steps per cycle (16 = sixteenth notes in a 4/4 bar)

random.description: largest random timing offset per step, in grid steps

seed.description: seed for the per-step random offsets

timing.description:
per-step timing offset in grid steps (positive = late); the template
repeats every `timing.length` steps

velocity.description: per-step velocity (0–1), one per `timing` entry; every step is 1 when empty

velocityAmount.description: velocity strength (0 = every step full, 1 = as written)

outputs.name: offset
outputs.description: how far the groove shifts the playhead, in cycles; pass to a sequencer's `groove`

outputs.name: velocity
outputs.description: velocity of the current groove step; pass to a sequencer's `velocity`

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: fires at the start of each grooved step

signalParams.name: playhead
signalParams.description: straight playhead to groove, in cycles; follows the global clock (without its groove) by default

name: $midiCV
documentation:
Converts MIDI note input into control voltages for driving synthesizer modules.
Supports polyphonic voice allocation with up to 64 voices.

## Outputs

| Output | Signal | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `pitch` | V/Oct pitch (0V = C4), includes pitch bend | — |
| `gate` | High while a note is held | 0–5V |
| `velocity` | Note-on velocity | 0–5V |
| `aftertouch` | Channel or polyphonic aftertouch | 0–5V |
| `retrigger` | 5V pulse for 1ms on each new note | 0–5V |
| `pitchWheel` | Pitch bend wheel position | -5V–+5V |
| `modWheel` | Mod wheel (CC 1) | 0–5V |

## Polyphonic modes (`polyMode`)

- `"rotate"` — cycles through voices round-robin
- `"reuse"` — reuses the voice that last played the same note
- `"reset"` — always starts allocation from voice 1
- `"mpe"` — one voice per MIDI channel (for MPE controllers)

## Monophonic modes (`monoMode`, when `channels: 1`)

- `"last"` — most recently pressed note wins
- `"first"` — first pressed note wins
- `"lowest"` — lowest held note wins
- `"highest"` — highest held note wins

## Example

```js
// 4-voice polyphonic MIDI synth
const midi = $midiCV({ channels: 4 });
$sine(midi).amplitude($adsr(midi.gate,{attack: 0.01, decay: 0.1, sustain: 0.8, release: 0.5})).out();

// Mono lead with pitch bend
const lead = $midiCV({ channels: 1, pitchBendRange: 12 });
$saw(lead).amplitude($adsr(lead.gate,{attack: 0.01, decay: 0.1, sustain: 0.8, release: 0.5})).out();
```

channel.description: MIDI channel to listen to; every channel when unset

device.description: MIDI device to listen to; every device when unset

monoMode.description: which held note plays when `channels` is 1

pitchBendRange.description: how far the pitch wheel bends, in semitones; 0 turns bending off

polyMode.description: how new notes are given to voices

oneOf.description: First note pressed wins (ignores new notes)

PolyMode.description: Voice allocation mode for polyphonic operation

oneOf.description: Reuse voice playing same note before rotating
Always start from the first voice
MPE mode: MIDI channel maps directly to output channel

outputs.description: pitch of the voice's note, including pitch bend

outputs.name: gate
outputs.description: high while the voice's note is held

outputs.name: velocity
outputs.description: how hard the note was struck

outputs.description: fires at the start of each new note, even when gate stays high

outputs.description: pitch wheel position: 0 centred, ±5 at either end

name: $grains
documentation:
Granular sampler. Continuously spawns short, windowed grains from a WAV
file, enabling time-stretching, pitch-shifting independent of time, and
cloud textures.

Each polyphonic channel maintains up to 64 concurrent grains. Spawned grains
capture their pitch, start position, and length at spawn time, so live
parameter changes only affect new grains.

Amplitude is normalised using the Mutable Instruments Clouds formula:
`gain = 1/√(max(1, smoothed_active_grains − 1))`.

```js
$grains('c4', $wavs().pad, $pulse('2hz'))
const seq = $cycle($p('c3 e3'))
$grains(seq, $wavs().strings, seq.gate, { density: 3, shape: 'bell', length: 2 })
```

density.description: how often grains spawn: 10 grains per second per volt

directionBias.description: chance a grain plays in reverse: 0 never, 5 always

gate.description: grains spawn while high; each new gate restarts the `loopCount` tally

length.description: grain length: 1 is 100 ms, 10 is 1 s, up to the length of the file

loopCount.description: how many grains each gate spawns; unlimited when unset

pitch.description: pitch of new grains: 0 plays at the file's own speed, each volt an octave

start.description: where in the file new grains start: 0 the beginning, 5 the end

GrainShape.description: Amplitude windowing function applied to each grain.

oneOf.description: Symmetric triangle: linear rise and fall meeting at the centre.
Linear rise to peak then a sharp 1 ms linear fall at the tail.
1 ms linear attack, sustain at peak, 1 ms linear decay.
1 ms linear attack followed by exponential decay matching `$perc`.

outputs.description: the mix of all playing grains

Plays the audio track of a media file in a loop, at a fixed speed, from
the loop start when the patch starts. The DSL creates one for each
`$v.video(...).audio`.

name: $sampler
documentation:
Sample player. Each gate rising edge starts playback of the whole file,
or of one slice when `slice` is set. The slice signal is sampled at the
edge: integer part picks the slice point (wrapping), fraction offsets the
start into it. `mode` sets what the gate does next: `'once'` plays the
window through, `'gate'` plays it while the gate is high, and `'loop'`
repeats it while the gate is high, picking the slice again for each
repeat. Speed control allows pitch-shifting and reverse playback (a slice
plays the same region backwards). A short `fade` (milliseconds) declicks
onsets, slice ends, releases, and retriggers.

```js
$sampler($wavs().kick, $clock.beatTrigger)
$sampler($wavs().pad, $pulse('1hz'), { speed: 0.5, mode: 'gate' })
$sampler($wavs().pad, $pulse('2hz'), { slice: [[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75], $cycle($p('0 1 2 3')).cv], fade: 2 })
$sampler($wavs().pad, $pulse('0.5hz'), { mode: 'loop', fade: 10 })
```

fade.description: declick fade in milliseconds, at the start and end of each pass, on release and across retriggers; 0 turns it off

gate.description: starts the selected slice playing; `mode` sets what the gate does after that

mode.description: what the gate does once playback starts

slice.description: which slice plays: a signal (the whole file is one slice) or `[points, signal]`, points marking slice starts as fractions of the file from 0 to 1; read at each gate and each loop repeat, its whole part picks the slice (wrapping) and its fraction starts partway in

speed.description: playback speed: 1 normal, 2 double (an octave up), negative plays in reverse

oneOf.description: each gate plays the slice through; the gate falling does nothing

the slice repeats in time while the gate is high, picking the slice
again at each repeat, and fades out over `fade` when the gate falls

the slice plays while the gate is high and fades out over `fade` when
it falls

name: $unstable.shape.saturate
documentation:
Saturation and clipping, from Surge XT's Saturator waveshapers. `mode`
sets the character — soft, hard, asymmetric, medium, or ojd — and `drive`
sets how hard the signal is pushed in (−5..5, 0 = unity).

## Example
```js
$unstable.shape.saturate($saw('c3'), 'hard', 3).out()
```

input.description: signal to shape; ±5 V spans the shaper's curve

oneOf.description: Asymmetric saturation — adds even harmonics for a warmer colour.
Medium saturation — sits between soft and hard.
Overdrive with a soft knee before it clips.
